by_task.when: ARIZONA is allowable and the facts establish wearing apparel, a musical instrument for individual or family use, a firearm, a motor vehicle, a professionally prescribed prosthesis or respiratory or mobility aid, or a domestic animal or household pet.
by_task.procedure: Use § 33-1125(1), (2), (10), (8), (9), or (11), respectively, even when the asset value exceeds a stated ceiling; a ceiling limits EV, not EC eligibility. Apply § 33-1123 only to household furniture, furnishings, goods, consumer electronics, or appliances.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not classify jewelry as wearing apparel or household property; only an expressly identified engagement or wedding ring uses § 33-1125(4). Do not substitute § 33-1123 for a musical instrument or prescribed medical aid. A burial plot is not an Arizona homestead; § 33-1101(A) requires a qualifying dwelling used as a residence.

by_task.when: ARIZONA is allowable and one of those category provisions is being valued.
by_task.procedure: Before calculating an amount, verify category eligibility: jewelry is outside § 33-1123, and jewelry not expressly identified as an engagement or wedding ring has no Arizona alternative under the supplied statutes. For each eligible asset-exemption pair independently, use the lesser of asset value and $2,000 under § 33-1125(10), or $15,000 under § 33-1125(8). Apply § 33-1125(1) only to actual wearing apparel, § 33-1125(4) only to an expressly identified engagement or wedding ring, § 33-1125(9) to a professionally prescribed prosthesis or medically required mobility or respiratory aid, and § 33-1125(11) to a domestic animal or household pet. Apply § 33-1123 only to household furniture, furnishings, goods, consumer electronics, or appliances.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not place a prescribed medical aid under § 33-1123, and do not use a cap as an eligibility test.

by_task.when: FEDERAL is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned property.
by_task.procedure: Include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) for every asset as an independent alternative, then add every factually matching category-specific federal exemption. The asset's value never defeats § 522(d)(5) eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 522(d)(5) because another subsection applies or because value exceeds $1,475. Do not report § 522(m), classify jewelry or a firearm under § 522(d)(3), or add federal law when FEDERAL is not allowable.

by_task.when: FEDERAL is an allowable jurisdiction and an independently applicable § 522(d)(5) alternative must be valued.
by_task.procedure: For each asset independently, claim the lesser of its value and $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of unused § 522(d)(1) capacity. Merely reporting § 522(d)(1) as another independent alternative does not consume that capacity; absent express facts showing actual consumption, use $15,425 for one debtor or $30,850 for two debtors. Also value § 522(d)(3) at the lesser of the asset value and $700 only for its enumerated categories, and use § 522(d)(4), not § 522(d)(3), for jewelry.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not allocate the wildcard across assets, infer consumption from another independently reported alternative, cap it at $1,475 without supporting facts, report § 522(m) itself, exceed the asset value, or classify jewelry or a firearm under § 522(d)(3).

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
by_task.procedure: First include 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) for every such asset. Then independently add subsection (a) for necessary wearing apparel, (c) for a motor vehicle, or (e) for a professionally prescribed health aid when that category is established.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not drop subsection (b) because a specific subsection also applies. Do not infer subsection (d) trade use from an item's name, classify jewelry as wearing apparel, or apply these personal-property exemptions to expressly business-use property.

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
by_task.procedure: Test § 5/12-1001(b) for every such asset, including property also covered by subsection (a), (c), or (e). Claim the lesser of asset value and $4,000 for one debtor; for jointly owned property in a two-debtor case use the lesser of asset value and $8,000. Include subsection (b) independently from every factually established specific subsection.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use the $4,000 single-debtor ceiling for jointly owned property, substitute subsection (b)'s ceiling for the separate motor-vehicle cap, infer subsection (d) trade use from an item's name, classify jewelry as wearing apparel, or apply these exemptions to expressly business-use property.

by_task.when: OREGON is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property.
by_task.procedure: Always include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p), even when a specific Oregon category also applies. Independently add (a) for books, pictures, or musical instruments; (b) for apparel or jewelry; (d) for vehicles; (e) for domestic animals or poultry; (f) for household goods, furniture, radios, televisions, or utensils; or (h) for professionally prescribed health aids.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit the catchall because a specific category applies, classify an animal under household-goods subsection (f), apply subsection (p) to real property, or add an Oregon category whose factual condition is absent.

by_task.when: An Oregon exemption alternative must be valued.
by_task.procedure: For § 18.345(1)(p), claim the lesser of asset value and $400 and retain every separately matching category provision. Use the lesser of value and $1,800 under § 18.345(1)(b), $3,000 under § 18.345(1)(d) or (f), and $1,000 for one firearm under § 18.362. For a homestead use § 18.395(1), not the personal-property catchall, with a $40,000 ceiling for one debtor or $50,000 when two household debtors' interests are subject to execution.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use any cap as an eligibility test or as a minimum claim, omit a matching category because the catchall applies, apply § 18.345(1)(p) to real property, or substitute an unrelated category. Never claim more than the asset value.

by_task.when: PENNSYLVANIA is allowable and the asset is property of the debtor.
by_task.procedure: Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 as an independent alternative for every kind of debtor property, whether or not a federal or specific Pennsylvania exemption also applies. A property's value above the statutory ceiling limits the EV amount but never defeats § 8123 eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not restrict § 8123 to cash, low-value, or uncategorized property. Apply § 8124(a)(1) only to actual wearing apparel, never to jewelry, animals, vehicles, furniture, appliances, or other non-clothing property; do not invent a Pennsylvania firearm or general-jewelry exemption.

by_task.when: An independently applicable Pennsylvania § 8123 alternative must be valued.
by_task.procedure: Test § 8123 for every debtor-owned property and always claim the lesser of the asset value and $300 for one debtor or $600 for jointly owned property in a two-debtor case.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 8123 because another exemption applies, allocate it across assets, use the ceiling when the asset is worth less, or reduce a joint ceiling to $300. Apply § 8124(a)(1) only to actual wearing apparel; do not invent a Pennsylvania firearm or general-jewelry provision.

Apply § 33-1125(1) only to actual wearing apparel, § 33-1125(4) only to an expressly identified engagement or wedding ring, § 33-1125(9) to a professionally prescribed prosthesis or medically required mobility or respiratory aid, and § 33-1125(11) to a domestic animal or household pet. Apply § 33-1123 only to household furniture, furnishings, goods, consumer electronics, or appliances.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not place a prescribed medical aid under § 33-1123, and do not use a cap as an eligibility test.

by_task.when: FEDERAL is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned property.
by_task.procedure: Include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) for every asset as an independent alternative, then add every factually matching category-specific federal exemption. The asset's value never defeats § 522(d)(5) eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 522(d)(5) because another subsection applies or because value exceeds $1,475. Do not report § 522(m), classify jewelry or a firearm under § 522(d)(3), or add federal law when FEDERAL is not allowable.

by_task.when: FEDERAL is an allowable jurisdiction and an independently applicable § 522(d)(5) alternative must be valued.
by_task.procedure: For each asset independently, claim the lesser of its value and $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of unused § 522(d)(1) capacity. Merely reporting § 522(d)(1) as another independent alternative does not consume that capacity; absent express facts showing actual consumption, use $15,425 for one debtor or $30,850 for two debtors. Also value § 522(d)(3) at the lesser of the asset value and $700 only for its enumerated categories, and use § 522(d)(4), not § 522(d)(3), for jewelry.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not allocate the wildcard across assets, infer consumption from another independently reported alternative, cap it at $1,475 without supporting facts, report § 522(m) itself, exceed the asset value, or classify jewelry or a firearm under § 522(d)(3).

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
by_task.procedure: First include 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) for every such asset. Then independently add subsection (a) for necessary wearing apparel, (c) for a motor vehicle, or (e) for a professionally prescribed health aid when that category is established.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not drop subsection (b) because a specific subsection also applies. Do not infer subsection (d) trade use from an item's name, classify jewelry as wearing apparel, or apply these personal-property exemptions to expressly business-use property.

by_task.when: ILLINOIS is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
by_task.procedure: Test § 5/12-1001(b) for every such asset, including property also covered by subsection (a), (c), or (e). Claim the lesser of asset value and $4,000 for one debtor; for jointly owned property in a two-debtor case use the lesser of asset value and $8,000. Include subsection (b) independently from every factually established specific subsection.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use the $4,000 single-debtor ceiling for jointly owned property, substitute subsection (b)'s ceiling for the separate motor-vehicle cap, infer subsection (d) trade use from an item's name, classify jewelry as wearing apparel, or apply these exemptions to expressly business-use property.

by_task.when: OREGON is allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property.
by_task.procedure: Always include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p), even when a specific Oregon category also applies. Independently add (a) for books, pictures, or musical instruments; (b) for apparel or jewelry; (d) for vehicles; (e) for domestic animals or poultry; (f) for household goods, furniture, radios, televisions, or utensils; or (h) for professionally prescribed health aids.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit the catchall because a specific category applies, classify an animal under household-goods subsection (f), apply subsection (p) to real property, or add an Oregon category whose factual condition is absent.

by_task.when: An Oregon exemption alternative must be valued.
by_task.procedure: For § 18.345(1)(p), claim the lesser of asset value and $400 and retain every separately matching category provision. Use the lesser of value and $1,800 under § 18.345(1)(b), $3,000 under § 18.345(1)(d) or (f), and $1,000 for one firearm under § 18.362. For a homestead use § 18.395(1), not the personal-property catchall, with a $40,000 ceiling for one debtor or $50,000 when two household debtors' interests are subject to execution.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use any cap as an eligibility test or as a minimum claim, omit a matching category because the catchall applies, apply § 18.345(1)(p) to real property, or substitute an unrelated category. Never claim more than the asset value.

by_task.when: PENNSYLVANIA is allowable and the asset is property of the debtor.
by_task.procedure: Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 as an independent alternative for every kind of debtor property, whether or not a federal or specific Pennsylvania exemption also applies. A property's value above the statutory ceiling limits the EV amount but never defeats § 8123 eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not restrict § 8123 to cash, low-value, or uncategorized property. Apply § 8124(a)(1) only to actual wearing apparel, never to jewelry, animals, vehicles, furniture, appliances, or other non-clothing property; do not invent a Pennsylvania firearm or general-jewelry exemption.

by_task.when: An independently applicable Pennsylvania § 8123 alternative must be valued.
by_task.procedure: Test § 8123 for every debtor-owned property and always claim the lesser of the asset value and $300 for one debtor or $600 for jointly owned property in a two-debtor case.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not omit § 8123 because another exemption applies, allocate it across assets, use the ceiling when the asset is worth less, or reduce a joint ceiling to $300. Apply § 8124(a)(1) only to actual wearing apparel; do not invent a Pennsylvania firearm or general-jewelry provision.

by_task.when: ARIZONA is allowable and the facts establish wearing apparel, a musical instrument for individual or family use, a firearm, a motor vehicle, a professionally prescribed prosthesis or respiratory or mobility aid, or a domestic animal or household pet.
by_task.procedure: Use § 33-1125(1), (2), (10), (8), (9), or (11), respectively, even when the asset value exceeds a stated ceiling; a ceiling limits EV, not EC eligibility. Apply § 33-1123 only to household furniture, furnishings, goods, consumer electronics, or appliances.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not classify jewelry as wearing apparel or household property; only an expressly identified engagement or wedding ring uses § 33-1125(4). Do not substitute § 33-1123 for a musical instrument or prescribed medical aid. A burial plot is not an Arizona homestead; § 33-1101(A) requires a qualifying dwelling used as a residence.

operations.rationale: In current-parent EV observations 183 and 248, the actor added § 33-1123 to non-ring jewelry, creating full-output false positives even though the released targets contain no Arizona alternative. Observation 207 confirms that only an expressly identified engagement or wedding ring may use § 33-1125(4). The revision makes category eligibility precede valuation while preserving the existing unrelated Arizona boundaries.
